item.title: Family Firms as Context for Organizational Behavior Processes
item.content:encoded:
Cristina Cruz, Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona

Luis Gomez-Mejia, Arizona State University

Justin Craig, University of Alberta

Family firms represent a significant and distinct organizational context that shapes how people behave, interact, and perform within organizations. Despite their prevalence globally and their substantial economic impact, family firms remain understudied in organizational behavior research. The unique characteristics of family firms—including family involvement in ownership and management, overlapping family and business systems, long-term orientations, and preservation of family legacy—create a distinctive context that influences organizational behavior processes in ways that differ fundamentally from non-family firms.

This special issue seeks to advance our understanding of how family firm contexts shape organizational behavior. We invite empirical and theoretical contributions that examine organizational behavior processes—including but not limited to motivation, leadership, organizational culture, change management, conflict resolution, team dynamics, organizational learning, and employee well-being—within family firm settings. We are particularly interested in research that illuminates the mechanisms through which family dynamics, governance structures, ownership arrangements, and family values influence these organizational behavior processes.

We welcome quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies that provide novel insights into organizational behavior in family firms. Submissions may focus on family firms of any size or industry, and may examine intra-organizational dynamics as well as family firm interactions with external stakeholders. We are especially interested in research that addresses underexplored questions, applies novel theoretical perspectives, or challenges conventional wisdom about family firms and organizational behavior.

Potential topics

  • How do family dynamics (e.g., family conflict, cohesion, intergenerational relationships) shape organizational behavior processes?
  • How do family ownership structures and governance arrangements influence employee motivation, commitment, and organizational culture?
  • How do succession planning and leadership transitions in family firms affect organizational behavior outcomes?
  • What is the role of family social capital and networks in shaping organizational behavior processes?
  • How do family firm values and mission influence employee behavior, organizational identity, and stakeholder relationships?
  • What are the implications of family involvement in management for organizational learning, innovation, and change processes?
  • How do family firms balance family interests with organizational effectiveness and employee well-being?
  • What role does emotional attachment to the firm play in shaping organizational behavior in family contexts?
  • How do family firm characteristics influence diversity, inclusion, and equity in organizational practices?
  • What are the unique challenges and opportunities for managing organizational behavior in multigenerational family firms?

Timeline

  • February 1, 2027: Full paper submission deadline

item.title: Governance in Family Firms: In Search of New Paradigms?
item.content:encoded:
This Special Issue seeks to advance theory and evidence on the evolution and response of governance systems in family firms to contemporary challenges such as the rise of public intervention in the economy, the advent of AI, and geopolitical turmoil. The special issue invites contributions that examine how governance mechanisms - including boards of directors, ownership structures, executive leadership, succession arrangements, and family governance systems - shape the ability of family firms to create value, preserve continuity, and adapt to changing environments.

Potential topics

  • Evolution and response of governance systems in family firms to contemporary challenges
  • Rise of public intervention in the economy
  • Advent of AI
  • Geopolitical turmoil
  • Boards of directors
  • Ownership structures
  • Executive leadership
  • Succession arrangements
  • Family governance systems
  • Value creation in family firms
  • Continuity preservation in family firms
  • Adaptation to changing environments

Timeline

  • January 15, 2027: Deadline for proposal submissions
